nham-tram-ha-chau.name: Ha Chau Black Canarium and Grilled Carp Platter
aliases: Thai Nguyen Nham with Black Canarium
nham-tram-ha-chau.serving_basis: Four portions served with rice crackers or nhoi leaves as a mixed dish for a family meal.
nham-tram-ha-chau.description: A Ha Chau specialty combining softened black canarium, fully cooked grilled carp, grilled pork belly, young banana stem, coconut, sour starfruit and aromatic leaves. Bếp Việt edits this version to use thoroughly cooked fish and a measured amount of fermented rice soy sauce for a balanced nutty, tangy and herbal flavor.
nham-tram-ha-chau.finished_dish: The canarium remains soft but intact, with fragrant grilled fish and pork, lightly crisp banana stem, and a balanced savory-tart dressing.
nham-tram-ha-chau.serving: Serve on a platter with toasted rice crackers or nhoi and fig leaves; offer extra Uc Ky fermented rice soy sauce on the side.
tips: Simmer the canarium gently until tender before removing the pits so the flesh stays intact.
Grill the carp and pork until fully cooked; cool slightly before flaking and mixing.
Add the fermented soy sauce and vinegar gradually to preserve the canarium’s nutty flavor.
nham-tram-ha-chau.image_alt: A Ha Chau platter of softened black canarium, fully cooked grilled carp, pork belly, young banana stem, coconut, sour starfruit and fresh leaves, served with rice crackers.
nham-tram-ha-chau.time_note: About 70 minutes; simmering and grilling times vary with ingredient size.
suggested_pairings: Uc Ky fermented rice soy sauce

ingredients.name: Black canarium fruit
ingredients.notes: Choose mature fruit and rinse well.

ingredients.name: Young banana stem
ingredients.notes: Shred and soak briefly in salted water.

ingredients.name: Sour starfruit
ingredients.notes: Remove hard edges and slice thinly.

ingredients.name: Local edible leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse and reserve a few for wrapping.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For seasoning the fish and pork.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Brush lightly on the fish and pork.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Remove seeds and slice; adjust to taste.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse and drain the canarium. Gently simmer in hot water until tender but not falling apart. Cool, remove the pits and chop the flesh.
Season the carp and pork belly with salt for 10 minutes. Rinse and slice the banana stem and starfruit; wash and drain the aromatic leaves.
Toast the sesame seeds and coarsely crush the peanuts. Set out the fermented soy sauce, vinegar and chili.

cooking_steps.instruction: Grill the carp and pork belly until the fish is opaque throughout and the pork is cooked through with lightly browned edges. Cool slightly, then flake the fish and remove any bones.
Combine the canarium, banana stem, coconut, starfruit, fish and pork in a bowl. Add the fermented soy sauce and vinegar gradually, mixing gently.
Fold in the aromatic leaves, sesame, peanuts and chili. Taste and adjust the savory-tart balance, then serve with rice crackers or nhoi leaves.

ca-linh-kho-lat-mien-tay.name: Mekong Delta Braised Linh Fish (Seasonal Freshwater Fish)
aliases: Mekong Delta Linh Fish in a Light Broth
ca-linh-kho-lat-mien-tay.serving_basis: Four portions served with steamed rice and a platter of Mekong Delta greens.
ca-linh-kho-lat-mien-tay.description: Linh fish is gently braised in a lightly seasoned broth with a little pork fat, pepper and shallot, preserving the fish’s natural sweetness. It is commonly enjoyed with rice and seasonal field vegetables such as water lily stems, bean sprouts, sesbania flowers and herbs.
ca-linh-kho-lat-mien-tay.finished_dish: The fish is tender but intact in a clear, lightly salty broth fragrant with pepper and shallot, served with crisp greens.
ca-linh-kho-lat-mien-tay.serving: Serve in a clay pot or deep platter with hot rice, water lily stems, bean sprouts, sesbania flowers, herbs and lime.
tips: Use fresh linh fish and clean it gently to avoid bruising.
Once the pot simmers, lower the heat and gently shake the pot instead of stirring.
Season lightly at first and adjust near the end because fish sauce varies in saltiness.
ca-linh-kho-lat-mien-tay.image_alt: Mekong Delta linh fish gently braised with shallot, pepper and a light savory broth, served with rice and seasonal greens.
ca-linh-kho-lat-mien-tay.time_note: About 70 minutes including 10 minutes of marinating; braising time depends on fish size.

ingredients.name: Fresh linh fish
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh fish; remove gills and entrails.

ingredients.name: Pork fat
ingredients.notes: Dice and render; reserve the cracklings.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Cut into short lengths; reserve the white parts.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For a light braising broth; add more if needed.

ingredients.name: Water lily stems
ingredients.notes: Peel fibers, cut and rinse for serving.

ingredients.name: Sesbania flowers
ingredients.notes: Pick and rinse when in season.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Use suitable fresh herbs, rinsed and drained.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: Cut into wedges for the greens.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse the linh fish briefly, remove the gills and entrails, and drain. Marinate with fish sauce, sugar, shallot, pepper and chili for 10 minutes.
Render the pork fat until the cracklings are golden; reserve the fat and cracklings. Rinse and drain the water lily stems, bean sprouts, sesbania flowers and herbs.

cooking_steps.instruction: Place the fish in a pot with the shallot marinade, fish sauce and water. Bring just to a simmer and skim any foam.
Lower the heat and add the rendered pork fat and cracklings. Braise gently for 20–25 minutes, occasionally shaking the pot instead of stirring so the fish stays intact.
Taste and adjust the lightly seasoned broth with salt or fish sauce. Add scallions and pepper; turn off the heat when the fish is tender and cooked through.
Serve hot with steamed rice and the prepared fresh vegetables; squeeze lime over the greens if desired.

ba-khia-rang-me-rach-goc.name: Rach Goc Mud Crab Stir-Fried with Tamarind
aliases: Ca Mau Mangrove mud crab with Tamarind
Rach Goc Mangrove mud crab in Tamarind Sauce
ba-khia-rang-me-rach-goc.serving_basis: Four portions as a shared snack or a savory dish for a family meal.
ba-khia-rang-me-rach-goc.description: Cleaned mangrove mud crabs are stir-fried until cooked through, then coated in a tamarind, garlic and chili glaze. The tangy sauce clings to the claws, shells and roe. Bếp Việt balances the sweet, salty and sour notes for rice or a shared plate.
ba-khia-rang-me-rach-goc.finished_dish: The mud crabs are fully cooked and firm, evenly coated in a glossy tamarind sauce with balanced sweet, salty and sour notes and fragrant garlic.
ba-khia-rang-me-rach-goc.serving: Finish with scallions and Vietnamese coriander. Serve hot with steamed rice or bread, with a crab pick for the claws.
tips: Choose fresh, intact mangrove mud crab and scrub mud from the shell and claws.
Cook the crabs thoroughly; never taste uncooked sauce that has touched raw seafood.
Taste the crabs before adding fish sauce because some may already be salted.
search_terms: mangrove mud crab in tamarind sauce
ba-khia-rang-me-rach-goc.image_alt: Rach Goc mangrove mud crabs stir-fried with tamarind, garlic and chili in a glossy sauce.
ba-khia-rang-me-rach-goc.time_note: About 45 minutes; cleaning time depends on whether the crabs are pre-cleaned.

ingredients.name: Fresh mangrove mud crab
ingredients.notes: Use fresh crabs, cleaned or whole for home cleaning.

ingredients.name: Ripe tamarind
ingredients.notes: Soak in warm water and strain.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the tartness of the tamarind.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use sparingly because the crab may be salty.

preparation_steps.instruction: If using whole crabs, scrub mud from the shells and claws, remove the apron, separate the top shell and halve the body; reserve roe if present. Rinse and drain.
Soak the tamarind in warm water and strain out the seeds. Mince the garlic and chili; mix the tamarind juice with sugar and fish sauce.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil and saute the garlic until fragrant. Add the mangrove mud crab and stir briefly over medium heat.
Pour in the tamarind mixture, turn to coat, cover and cook until the crabs are fully cooked, the flesh is opaque and the center is hot.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until it thickly coats the crabs. Add reserved roe and cook it through, then taste for a balanced sour-sweet-salty flavor.
Turn off the heat, add pepper, scallions and Vietnamese coriander, and serve hot.

de-tai-chanh-ninh-binh.name: Ninh Binh Fully Cooked Goat with Lime
aliases: Goat with Lime, Lemongrass and Sesame
de-tai-chanh-ninh-binh.serving_basis: Four portions served with herbs, fig leaves, green banana and fermented soybean dip.
de-tai-chanh-ninh-binh.description: A Ninh Binh mountain-goat specialty traditionally made by steaming the goat until cooked, then tossing it with lime juice, lemongrass, galangal and toasted sesame. Bếp Việt keeps the familiar “lime-marinated goat” dish name but provides a fully cooked version with no raw or pink meat.
de-tai-chanh-ninh-binh.finished_dish: The goat is tender and fully cooked with no pink center; lime is bright but gentle, lemongrass and galangal are balanced, and toasted sesame adds nuttiness.
de-tai-chanh-ninh-binh.serving: Serve with fig leaves, Vietnamese balm, fresh herbs and thinly sliced green banana; dip in fermented soybean sauce or ginger fish sauce.
tips: “Lime-marinated goat” is the traditional dish name; this Bếp Việt version steams the meat fully.
Check the thickest center with a food thermometer. USDA recommends at least 63C for whole cuts of goat; this recipe targets about 71C for a well-done result.
Add lime only after the goat is cooked; citrus does not replace cooking.
de-tai-chanh-ninh-binh.image_alt: Fully cooked Ninh Binh mountain goat tossed with lime juice, lemongrass, galangal and toasted sesame.
de-tai-chanh-ninh-binh.time_note: About 85 minutes including 20 minutes of marinating; steam the goat thoroughly before adding lime.

ingredients.name: Lean goat meat
ingredients.notes: Use leg or shoulder and cut into even blocks.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Bruise; use some to line the steamer and slice the rest.

ingredients.name: Galangal
ingredients.notes: Slice half for steaming and julienne the rest.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Strain out the seeds and add gradually.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Seed and slice; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Green banana
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly and soak in salted lime water.

preparation_steps.instruction: Keep the goat chilled while preparing it. Cut into evenly sized blocks, rinse briefly, rub with salt and ginger, rinse again and pat dry.
Marinate with salt, half the lemongrass and galangal for 20 minutes. Line the steamer with ginger, lemongrass and galangal.
Toast the sesame and shred the lime leaves and chili. Rinse the herbs; slice the green banana and soak it in salted lime water.

cooking_steps.instruction: Bring the steamer water to a boil. Arrange the goat in a loose layer, cover and steam until the thickest pieces are fully cooked with no pink center; target about 71C with a food thermometer and rest for 3 minutes.
Let the meat cool slightly, then slice across the grain. Toss gently with lemongrass, galangal, lime juice, fish sauce and sugar.
Fold in toasted sesame, lime leaves and chili. Taste for acidity and salt, then serve with fig leaves, herbs, green banana and fermented soybean sauce.

ca-tam-nuong-la-bang.name: La Bang Grilled Sturgeon
ca-tam-nuong-la-bang.serving_basis: Four portions served with fresh herbs, wrap vegetables and dipping sauce.
ca-tam-nuong-la-bang.description: Fresh sturgeon from the Suoi Kem area of La Bang is prepared in several local dishes, including grilled sturgeon. This Bếp Việt version marinates the fish with galangal, fermented rice, lemongrass and a little fish sauce, then grills it until opaque, fragrant and moist.
ca-tam-nuong-la-bang.finished_dish: The outside is lightly golden while the inside is opaque, moist and firm; galangal and lemongrass are fragrant and the fermented rice adds mild acidity.
ca-tam-nuong-la-bang.serving: Serve hot with lettuce, wild betel leaves, perilla, sour starfruit and green banana; offer salt-chili dip or a light fish sauce dip.
tips: Clean the slime with warm water and salt; avoid boiling water that can damage the fish surface.
Cut evenly thick pieces so they cook at the same rate; avoid over-grilling.
Marinate under refrigeration and discard any marinade that touched raw fish rather than serving it as a dip.
search_terms: sturgeon grilled with galangal and fermented rice
ca-tam-nuong-la-bang.image_alt: Grilled sturgeon marinated with galangal, fermented rice, lemongrass and fish sauce, served hot.
ca-tam-nuong-la-bang.time_note: About 100 minutes including 40 minutes of marinating; grilling time varies with thickness and equipment.

ingredients.name: Sturgeon fillet or steaks
ingredients.notes: Cut about 3 cm thick and clean off the slime.

ingredients.name: Green banana
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly and soak in salted lime water.

preparation_steps.instruction: Pour warm water, about 60–70°C, over the sturgeon and gently scrape away the slime. Rub with coarse salt and a little lime, rinse and pat dry. Cut into pieces about 3 cm thick.
Mix the galangal, lemongrass, fermented rice, fish sauce, sugar and oil. Coat the fish, cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 40 minutes.
Rinse the wrap vegetables, slice the starfruit and green banana, then drain. Preheat the oven or prepare medium-hot charcoal.

cooking_steps.instruction: Arrange the fish on a rack or lined baking tray. Grill at about 200°C, turning once after 12–15 minutes; total time is usually 20–25 minutes depending on thickness.
Cook until the surface is lightly golden and the flesh inside is opaque and flakes easily. For thick pieces, continue grilling a few minutes rather than raising the heat and scorching the outside.
Serve hot with lettuce, wild betel leaves, perilla, starfruit, green banana and your preferred dipping sauce.
